## cave-wall-pixel-v1.png — final prompt

Create a production PNG game texture using the attached existing PETOA rock sprite as STYLE REFERENCE. Output ONE square seamless cave rock wall tile, opaque edge-to-edge coverage, no margins, no text. Match the reference's carefully hand-painted retro JRPG pixel art: dark outlines, irregular chunky organic rocks, small crisp pixel clusters, nuanced limited gray slate palette with slightly warm highlights, top-left light. Remove moss and plants for an underground cave. Dense interlocking natural rock masses, turtle-shell-like bumpy polygonal rounded stones, deep narrow cracks, varied sizes, no bricks, no regular geometric hex grid, no crystals. Orthographic surface for a top-down RPG rock wall. All four edges tile seamlessly. Aim for the detail of a 96x96 pixel tile enlarged with nearest-neighbor: clearly deliberate pixel art, no smooth vector facets, no photorealism, no blur. Match existing reference texture craftsmanship.

## blue-bedrock-pixel-v1.png — final prompt

Create ONE production PNG game asset, wide horizontal cave wall panel aspect ratio about 3:1, for PETOA top-down retro JRPG. The attached mossy rock sprite is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY: match its organic detailed pixel-art rock shading, crisp pixel clusters, dark contours and top-left highlights. Main subject: continuous BLUE LUMINOUS BEDROCK made of thick bumpy interlocking stone plates resembling a turtle shell, irregular rounded polygonal rock masses with broad raised domes and many tiny weathered chips. Dark slate-blue rock, muted teal-blue facets and sparse luminous cyan narrow fissures. The entire wall is blue mineral rock. No tall pointed crystals, no crystal spikes, no bricks, no perfectly regular hexagonal tiles, no actual turtle, no plants. Rock face must fill the full width and height edge-to-edge with no surrounding scene, no floor, no black rectangle backdrop, no border or margins. Opaque densely packed wall surface suitable to join ordinary cave wall at its top and sides. Clearly crafted pixel art matching a 240x72 pixel game texture enlarged nearest-neighbor, rich hand-placed pixel shading as in reference, not vector shapes, not smooth 3D. No text. Emission should be detailed cyan pixels inside cracks, not blurry bloom.

## black-bedrock-pixel-v1.png

Generated with the built-in `image_gen` tool on 2026-09-14, using `blue-bedrock-pixel-v1.png` as the edit target. Original output preserved. Used for the next-morning rock wall and its journal image; a texture swap works in both Canvas and WebGL renderers.

Final prompt:

Use case: lighting-weather. Edit target: supplied pixel art blue cave bedrock texture. Create its exact next-morning state after all magic light has disappeared: the SAME rocks have turned BLACK. Preserve the composition, rock silhouettes, cracks, pixel grid, texture detail, framing, wide aspect ratio and opaque edge-to-edge rock coverage. Change ONLY color and emissive light. Remove ALL blue/cyan hues, glowing veins, glow and sparkle; veins become nearly black cracks. Use neutral black and charcoal gray stone with very subdued dark gray highlights so the rock forms remain readable against black crevices. No warm glow, no sunlight, no new objects, no text. This is an in-game texture swap for a retro pixel RPG, so it must read unmistakably as the same rock wall, now unlit black stone.
